summary: Client SDK connection leak + aggressive retry policy causing request surge and perceived inference slowdowns
description: Customer reported a sudden spike in end-to-end inference latency and increased request timeouts from their Dedicated deployment. Symptoms: 95th/99th token latency up ~3x, frequent 504/502 responses from the Redwood API, and application-side request queuing. Customer runs the Redwood JS SDK embedded in a serverless front-end with moderate concurrency (~200 rps).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's runtime reproducer: spawn 200 concurrent requests to /v1/chat with streaming enabled. 2) SDK version pinned to 2.1.2 with custom retry/backoff: maxRetries=6, baseBackoffMs=20, maxBackoffMs=150. 3) Observe connection counts on client host and error rates to Redwood endpoint. 4) Repeat under steady load for 15 minutes.
observed_logs: Customer app logs: repeated 'socket: reuse failed' and 'connection timed out' entries, a steady increase in TCP TIME_WAIT sockets, and app-level debug: 'retries exhausted -> returning 504'. On Redwood side: Gateway logs show a burst of HTTP 429/502 over a 90s window, followed by recovery. Sample gateway lines: '2026-03-05T14:12:21Z - svc-gateway - 502 - upstream read timeout', '2026-03-05T14:12:22Z - svc-gateway - 429 - rate limit - connection-pool-exhausted'.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: serving-runtime regression. Benchmarks on our fleet showed nominal tail latency for same model under similar load.
- Digging into customer environment: observed ephemeral port exhaustion on their host; socket counts grew linearly.
- Reproducer confirmed: the customer's usage pattern combined streaming responses with not awaiting/closing the stream iterator in their wrapper, causing TCP sockets to remain in TIME_WAIT longer.
- SDK review: version 2.1.2 had a bug in the HTTP connection pool where aborted streaming responses did not return connections to the pool under certain error paths. This increases per-host connection usage.
- Retry/backoff policy amplified the effect: customer's config retried quickly (baseBackoffMs=20, no jitter) and maxRetries=6, generating retry bursts that saturated the limited pool and triggered upstream 429s and 502s.
- Correlation: spikes in retries aligned with increases in socket counts and gateway 429s.
- Reproduction confirmed with an instrumented client: forcing a single connection leak path plus aggressive retries reproduced the perceived slowdown within 2-3 minutes.
comments: Support (Ayesha): Initial triage - escalated to Eng after customer provided tcpdump and SDK logs.
SRE (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed gateway 429s correspond to increased simultaneous connections from customer's IP; recommended customer throttle and restart app as immediate mitigation.

SDK Eng (Liam): Identified connection return path bug in 2.1.2; drafted patch to ensure aborted/consumed streaming responses always release connection to pool; added jitter to example retry policy in docs.
Customer (AtlasHealthAI - Devops): Applied temporary fix: restarted service and set concurrency cap to 50; saw immediate reduction in 5xxs and queue lengths.
Support (Ayesha): Verified latency returned to baseline after customer applied SDK patch and config change; marking resolved.
resolution:
Root cause: combination of a client-side connection return bug in SDK v2.1.2 and an aggressive retry/backoff configuration on the customer's side which together caused connection pool exhaustion and retry storms.
Actions taken: 1) SDK team released patch v2.1.4 to properly return connections on aborted/streamed responses (PR #984). 2) Provided customer with recommended runtime config: maxConnectionsPerHost >= 20, enable keep-alive, set maxRetries <= 3, baseBackoffMs 100-200 with jitter, and avoid un-awaited streaming iterator patterns. 3) Customer restarted service and deployed SDK v2.1.4; monitoring showed 95th/99th latency and error rates returned to baseline within 20 minutes.
Follow-ups: SDK team to add unit/integration tests for streaming abort paths (INT-1120), and update quickstart docs with explicit retry/backoff examples.
